passages.note: The enacted text cuts the main individual income tax rate but also amends unemployment insurance, property tax assessment ratios, urban revenue sharing, forest-product credits, school tuition organizations and fire district levy caps.

rows.reasoning: The only evidence is Marsh's No vote on SB1828 (2021), a bill captioned "omnibus; taxation" that amends unemployment benefit levels, property tax assessment ratios, urban revenue sharing, forest-product tax credits, school tuition organizations and fire district levy caps alongside the income tax rate change. A No vote on a multi-subject bill proves nothing about any one clause, so nothing here shows whether she would "Keep the current tax system mostly as-is, with targeted adjustments" or "Moderately raise taxes on wealthy people and large companies to fund existing services", and no surviving passage establishes a rung.
